title: docs(spec): the guardOf docblock and its test title state the has() rule that holds now
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoAbFvsoZdKGPS2souyWMqfZ)_

Fixes #25282

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

Two prose edits in `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts` and its test. No behaviour change.

- The `guardOf` docblock said `has()` refuses an index anywhere in its argument (`has(a[0].b)`, `has(vars["$x"].y)`). Since PR #25275 that is no longer true: `has()` refuses an index only as the **last** step of its argument, and an index before it is a presence test. The docblock now says that, and gives the reason the guard still skips a path with a numeric segment, a `$`-named head or a keyword segment: the guard tests every step of the path, each of those segments is read by index, so one of the guard's tests would end on that index.
- The test title "an index anywhere in the path leaves it unguarded — `has()` refuses one at run time" now reads "an index in the path leaves it unguarded — a step-at-a-time guard would end a `has()` on it, which `has()` refuses at run time". The assertions are unchanged.

## The rule, measured

Through `celEngine.evaluate` in `@objectstack/formula` at this head (a throwaway probe test, deleted after the run), with `vars = { rows: [{ name: 'a' }], $x: { y: 1 }, record: { in: 1 } }`:

| source | answer |
|---|---|
| `has(vars.rows[0].name)` | `ok: true`, `true` |
| `has(vars.rows[0].nope)` | `ok: true`, `false` |
| `has(vars["$x"].y)` | `ok: true`, `true` |
| `has(vars.rows[0])` | refused, `has() invalid argument` |
| `has(vars["$x"])` | refused, `has() invalid argument` |
| `has(vars.record["in"])` | refused, `has() invalid argument` |
| `has(vars.rows) && has(vars.rows[0]) && has(vars.rows[0].name)` (the guard's shape) | refused, `has() invalid argument` |

So the docblock's old examples are now accepted, and the guard the function would build for such a path still faults on its middle step. The behaviour (no guard) stays right; only the stated reason changed.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`. The file is `.ts`, not one of the `src/**/*.zod.ts` sources `@objectstack/spec` ships in `files[]`, and `guardOf` is module-private. Measured on the built `dist/` before the edit: the old docblock sentence ("takes a field selection over names alone") has 0 hits, while the same file's `ABSENT_SENTENCE` text (positive control) is present in `dist/automation/index.js`. The comment does not ship.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`, then `vitest run src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.test.ts` (Test Files 1 passed, Tests 172 passed), then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 79 commands. All were run with exit codes captured before any pipe; `--ran` reconciles: 79 derived, 78 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. All 78 run exited 0. Three first exited 3 on a missing prerequisite and were 0 on a rerun: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (after fetching its pinned fixture commit), `@objectstack/lint check:doc-formula-expressions` (after building formula and lint) and `check:lean-entry-closure` (after building objectql). NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, reason: it needs every package's `dist/`; left to CI.
- Dogfood: n/a (no `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm).
